issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Measurements value input rounds everything to 1 decimal, so quarter-inch steps are impossible and the displayed value drifts from what gets saved.

WHERE: src/pages/Measurements.tsx — displayMeasurement (line ~339) is parseFloat((measurement/2.54).toFixed(1)) in inch mode (1-decimal), but getStep() is 0.25 inch and the +/- handlers (lines ~561/570) compute the next value FROM the rounded display: setMeasurementFromDisplay(displayMeasurement + 0.25).

ACTUAL: (1) In inch mode, tapping + from 0 shows 0.3 -> 0.6 -> 0.8 -> 1.1 ... — uneven jumps, never the promised 0.25 increments, because each tap re-derives from the 1-decimal-rounded display. (2) Typing a 2-decimal value snaps: type 36.25 -> input immediately rewrites to 36.3. (3) Display vs saved diverge: after taps the label can read 0.80 inch while the canonical cm value saved to the backend is 2.159 cm = 0.85 inch (Save uses the unrounded 'measurement' state, line ~309). Same class of mismatch in cm mode: typing 40.25 cm shows 40.3 but saves 40.25.

EXPECTED: display keeps 2 decimals (matching the 0.25 step and the '0.00' placeholder/label which already use toFixed(2)); +/- should step the canonical value, not the rounded display, so the shown number always equals the saved number.

REPRO: /measurements -> toggle unit to 'inch' -> tap + three times from empty -> observe 0.30 / 0.60 / 0.80 instead of 0.25 / 0.50 / 0.75. Or type 36.25 in the value field -> it snaps to 36.3.

NOTE: distinct from i-20260704-22f4/0140 (stepper reset on background refetch — already fixed via userEdited ref); this is the display-rounding feedback loop.

issues.description:
[bug-hunt] Progress Photos: delete button is invisible and unreachable-by-sight on touch devices — it only appears on mouse hover, yet the app's primary platform is Android/Capacitor.

WHERE: src/components/measurements/ProgressPhotos.tsx (~line 252): the per-photo trash button is 'opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100 focus-visible:opacity-100'. Touch devices have no hover, so the control never becomes visible.

ACTUAL: on a phone there is NO visible way to delete a progress photo. Worse, the invisible button still receives taps (opacity-0 keeps pointer events), so tapping the top-right corner of a photo thumbnail opens the 'Delete photo?' dialog with no visible trigger — a hidden destructive control. The button is also 28x28px (w-7 h-7), violating the project's 44x44px touch-target rule.

EXPECTED: delete affordance always visible on touch (e.g. persistent small overlay button, or long-press/menu), min 44x44 target.

REPRO: open /measurements on a touch device (or Playwright mobile emulation, no hover) with at least 1 progress photo -> no delete icon visible on any thumbnail; tap the top-right corner of a thumbnail -> Delete confirmation appears out of nowhere.

issues.description: [suggestion] Exercise form-cue sheet: tap any exercise in a workout to see 3-4 concise form cues, common mistakes, and a breathing tip. USER PROBLEM: during a live workout the athlete sees only exercise name + sets×reps×RPE — zero guidance on how to actually perform the movement. Beginners (the walking_only/light tiers the app explicitly provisions for) either guess (injury + bad results) or leave the workout screen to ask the coach chat / Google, which kills the session flow and burns LLM rate-limit budget on a static question. EVIDENCE: a repo-wide grep finds NO instruction/video/form-cue content anywhere — the exercise catalog carries only equipment/sets/reps/RPE (ExercisePickerSheet, getAlternatives), and Activity.tsx's live-workout card renders no info affordance. Every comparable tracker (Hevy, Strong, Fitbod, cult.fit) ships per-exercise how-to as table stakes. V1 SCOPE: an info icon on the exercise card in the live workout (Activity.tsx) and in NextSessionPreview opens a calm bottom sheet with: 3-4 form cues, 2 common mistakes, 1 breathing tip. Content is LLM-generated ONCE per exercise server-side and cached in a new exercise_form_cues table (exercise_id → JSON), served via GET /api/v1/exercises/<id>/form-cues; first-request-generates, then cached forever — so LLM cost is one call per distinct exercise ever, not per user. No video, no images, no personalization in v1. EFFORT: ~2 days full-stack (1 endpoint + 1 table + migration; 1 bottom-sheet component + 2 tap targets). Zero impact on existing flows if the endpoint 404s (sheet just doesn't open).
issues.author: shakeebshaan

issues.description: [suggestion] Live 16:8 intermittent-fasting timer on the Nutrition page. USER PROBLEM: the app already lets users flag a fasting day (Vrat / Full fast / 16:8 window) but that is a STATIC boolean banner -- it only pauses meal reminders. It does not tell the user where they are IN the fast, which is the whole point of intermittent fasting: how long have I fasted, and when does my eating window open/close? Without a live count, 16:8 is unusable and users abandon it. EVIDENCE: FastingBanner in src/pages/Nutrition.tsx (~lines 47-100) offers a '16:8 window' type but renders no timer/countdown -- a grep shows zero fasting-timer / eating-window code, so the live feature is a genuine gap, not a duplicate. Intermittent fasting is a headline retention feature in every major tracker used in India (HealthifyMe, Zero, Fastic), and vrat/fasting is already culturally central to this India audience (the app even ships a 'Vrat / fruit-only' fast type). V1 SCOPE: when the user picks the '16:8 window' fast type, capture the fast-start timestamp and show a calm circular progress ring (reuse the existing teal ring vocabulary) with 'Xh Ym fasted', the eating-window open time, and a state label (Fasting / Eating window open). Client-side only, NO backend: persist fastStart + window config in localStorage keyed by date; the ring updates from a 1-min interval; the existing 'End fast' button clears it. Skip push reminders and fast history in v1. EFFORT: roughly 1-2 days frontend, no backend, no schema -- extends the fasting toggle already on Nutrition.

issues.description: [suggestion] Auto-generate a weekly grocery list from the assigned diet plan. USER PROBLEM: users get a 7-day plan (DietPlanWeek) but must manually work out what to buy to actually cook it — adherence dies at the grocery store, the biggest gap between having a plan and following it. EVIDENCE: the backend already serves per-ingredient data (name + quantity + unit) for every meal (RecipeDetail consumes recipe.ingredients); DietPlanWeek already loads the whole week. A grep shows zero existing grocery/shopping code, so this is a genuine gap. Comparable trackers (Mealime, Eat This Much, PlateJoy) ship auto grocery lists as a headline retention feature. V1 SCOPE: new route /diet-plan/shopping-list reached from a 'Shopping list' button on DietPlanWeek. Client-side only, NO backend change: flatten ingredients across the week's assigned meals, sum duplicates by normalised name+unit, sort alphabetically (skip a category taxonomy in v1), render a check-off list with checked state persisted in localStorage. Add one 'Copy as text / Share' button (WhatsApp-heavy India audience) so the list can be sent to whoever shops. EFFORT: roughly 1-2 days frontend, no backend, no schema. Reuses the existing diet-plan query and ingredient shape.

issues.reviewReason: Coach message fired at 3:55 AM local time — likely the APScheduler proactive message job dispatching at wrong local hour due to UTC vs IST offset. The scheduler runs in UTC; if the job is scheduled for 8am IST, it fires at 2:30am UTC which is 8am IST. But at 3:55am IST that would be ~10:25pm UTC the day before, suggesting a timezone offset bug. Owner-scope to fix (requires scheduler job timezone review in scheduler_jobs.py). Filed for tracking.
